sources.label: SEC cybersecurity disclosure rule
sources.intervalBecause: A disclosure clock, where the harm from a missed amendment is a LATE FILING and is asymmetric — nobody is penalised for reading the rule too often. The operative text of these instruments is comparatively stable; the staff interpretation around them is not, and it is the interpretation that moves a deadline. 365 days would let a changed clock sit unnoticed for up to a year on the one artifact whose value is being on time. Halved to 180 on 2026-08-09.

sources.label: DORA (Level 1)
sources.intervalBecause: Arts. 2 and 16 read in full against the EUR-Lex text on 2026-08-09 to settle which entities are excluded from inside the financial-entity list, and to establish that Art. 16 disapplies Arts. 5 to 15 only and does NOT reach the Chapter III reporting obligation. Three shipped receipts now carry that reading, and the wrong one - Art. 16 as an exemption from reporting - is a single plausible edit away. A change here makes a customer-facing receipt wrong rather than merely stale.

sources.label: FCC CPNI breach notification rule
sources.instrument: 47 CFR s 64.2011, Notification of customer proprietary network information security breaches
sources.version: Current as of 9 August 2026. Carriers notify USSS and FBI no later than 7 business days; customer notice waits 7 full business days after that, and an investigating agency may direct a further delay of up to 30 days, extendable.
